editorial:
Imagine waking up and realizing you have been doing wild things in your sleep that you can't explain. That is exactly what happens to Nathan in this wacky ride. After the madness of his previous adventures, he starts sleepwalking and decides to film himself to see what is going on. When things get way too weird, he brings in the only friend who can handle this kind of chaos. The whole vibe is like a home movie gone wrong, mixing goofy laughs with creepy monster moments that keep you guessing about what will happen next.

You will love how the movie keeps the energy high and doesn't take itself too seriously. The acting feels natural, and the practical effects for the creature are a huge plus. While the plot gets a bit messy toward the middle, the funny dialogue makes up for it. If you are into weird indie horror, you should definitely check this out. It looks great streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, but if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical shelf is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final act, it is revealed that the sleepwalking was actually a slow transformation into a primate beast. Nathan fights against his instincts in a big, messy brawl. After a chaotic struggle, the curse is finally broken through a lucky accident involving his friend. The movie ends with a funny joke suggesting that while the ape is gone, Nathan might still be prone to some very strange habits when he closes his eyes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves campy horror and weird comedies.
